title: A legacy Dropbox token value with no carrier, and a lone access_token member
summary: A synthetic value alone in prose, and an access_token member that stands alone in a JSON object with no token_type, account_id or uid.
rationale: Dropbox gives no prefix, alphabet or length for the legacy token and says access tokens are opaque, so a bare value has no carrier and cannot be separated from a short-lived token or other value by shape; the only difference the page shows is which members a response example carries. The pages also conflict on the retirement date (the guide's mid 2021 against the blog's 2021-09-30), no page says when creation actually stopped or when an existing token stops authenticating, and the single-artifact format lead was never corroborated by a second artifact. What is open is attribution to this family, not whether an opaque value is sensitive; the response-member Case does not depend on any of it.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted for this family: the format is not stated, the retirement-date statements conflict (claim retirement-date-statements-differ), the end of authentication of existing tokens is not stated, and a lone member or bare value cannot be separated from the short-lived token by any provider statement. A Dropbox statement of the format, of the date, or of what happens to existing tokens would settle it.

sources.supports: Long-lived access tokens are deprecated and remain available in the Developer console until mid 2021.
On September 30th, 2021 Dropbox will retire the creation of long-lived access tokens; the pages do not reconcile this date with the guide's and neither says when existing tokens stop authenticating.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. No outcome is asserted: the open question named in the expectation is what would have to be settled first.
